messages:
support_jen: Hey team, customer Acme reports sudden 503s across several requests starting ~10:20Z. sample request id: rq_0a1b2c3d. They see upstream inference failures, says it worked earlier this morning. Can eng-sre take a look?
ops-bot: Alert: hosted-infer-prod - 503 spike detected (10:21Z). Affected pool: hosted-gpu-2. Routing fallback triggered.
mike_chen: I'm the oncall, pulling logs now. any quick mitigation from support?
jonah_support: We already routed traffic to fallback models and informed the customer. They flagged a batch of toolcall requests with long contexts.
sara_reid: Looking at runner logs for instance id runner-0723, I see repeated process exits: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:20:19Z] infer-runner[pid:2345] SIGSEGV at 0x7f8b2c44
[2026-03-15T10:20:19Z] GPU OOM? free=128MB, required=450MB
[2026-03-15T10:20:19Z] kworker: container restart triggered
```
This smells like KV-prefetch memory spike leading to OOM then segfault during attention kernel.
alex_k: Repro attempt: running same request locally with batch size 4 and prefetch=on spikes vram on step 0. Kernel log shows assert in cuBLASLt. GDB backtrace attached: 
```
#0 0x7f8b2c44 in llt_matmul()
#1 0x7f8b3d11 in attention_forward()
#2 0x7f8b4a00 in run_infer()
```
mike_chen: Ok mitigation steps: 1) scale down prefetch window for hosted-gpu-2 pool, 2) temporarily route high-context toolcalls to dedicated fallback, 3) restart affected runner replicas gradually to avoid thundering herd. I'm going to bump prefetch limit to 64 tokens and roll restart.
deploy-bot: Change approved by oncall. Starting rolling restart set: hosted-gpu-2 (replicas=12) with maxUnavailable=2.
sara_reid: FYI stack traces show memory accounting mismatch when KV cache double-maps for hot-swap. Need to check allocator flags and nvml reports. nvml shows transient LRU eviction spikes before first crash.
jonah_support: Customer reports latency improved after fallback, but still sees occasional 503s; they want timeline and root cause.
alex_k: Short-term patch: disable aggressive KV prefetch for models with >32k context, and catch segfaults to fall back to safe execution path. I'll open a PR and submit canary.
sara_reid: Repro steps for engineering: 1) use sample payload (attached) with streaming toolcall and context ~48k tokens, 2) run against hosted-gpu-2 runner replica under load (qps=20) and watch nvml stats, 3) observe whether prefetch causes mem spike then SIGSEGV.
mike_chen: I've implemented the prefetch limit change and restarted 4/12 replicas. Error rate dropped from 6% -> 0.8% in the pool. Continuing rollout.
cs_escalations: Customer updated: primary app back to normal, still wants postmortem and ETA for fix. Please include mitigation and ETA.
sara_reid: We'll file an incident ticket with root cause = KV-prefetch memory spike + kernel assert leading to segfault. Owner: alex_k. ETA for soft fix (config guardrail) 3h, full runtime fix 2d.
alex_k: PR opened: disable aggressive prefetch for large-context models + guardrails + unit test. Canary will be deployed to hosted-gpu-2-canary in 40m.
mike_chen: Leaving note: monitor 503 rate, nvml memory high-water, and runner restart count. If we see another crash, escalate to infra for kernel dump capture.
support_jen: Thanks all — relaying update to customer. tagging for follow-up postmortem. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation in place, status=monitoring.
deploy-bot: Canary completed. No new crashes in canary after 1h.
sara_reid: Adding follow-up: need to audit allocator flags and add a throttling path for toolcalls that request very large prefetch windows. Filing JIRA: INF-8421.
cs_escalations: Customer acknowledged update and asks for timeline for runtime patch. will await 2d fix.
alex_k: Will post PR link and postmortem when work is complete.
